note: Video ideas for the planner, written by the research agent (agents/research.md). A video uses a topic once (plan.topic.feed_id); breaking topics go first.

topics.title: Indians put a record amount into SIPs in one month
topics.angle: The record is a crowd signal; what a single SIP of your own becomes is the story.
topics.why_now: AMFI's monthly data showed record gross SIP inflows; SIP numbers are widely shared and searched.
verify: AMFI's own monthly data (amfiindia.com) shows gross SIP inflows of ₹31,781 crore for June 2026
It was a record high when reported; if a later month is higher, say 'a record' only if still true, or update the fact
topics.reason: Superseded: AMFI published September 2026 data (record Rs 32,490 cr) on 2026-10-12; June figure is stale.

topics.title: RBI raises the repo rate for the first time since 2023
topics.angle: My home or car loan EMI: will it go up, and what happens to my FD rate?
topics.why_now: MPC raised repo by 25 bps on 7 Oct 2026 and moved to 'calibrated tightening'; everyone with a floating-rate loan is asking.

facts.label: RBI repo rate after the October policy

verify: RBI press release prid=63742 shows repo rate 5.50% after a 25 bps hike on 7 Oct 2026 (previously 5.25%)
Stance changed to 'calibrated tightening'; say 'first hike since Feb 2023' only if the RBI release or minutes confirm it
Do not claim the exact EMI change for any lender; floating loans reset per lender policy

topics.title: SIP money hit a new record in September, even as the market fell
topics.angle: Indians kept investing through a market dip; what does staying invested do for one SIP of yours?
topics.why_now: AMFI's September data (released 12 Oct) shows record SIP contributions while the Nifty fell nearly 6% in the month.
verify: AMFI monthly note (amfiindia.com) shows SIP contributions of Rs 32,490 crore for September 2026
It is described as a record; confirm no higher month
Skip the Nifty fall figure unless confirmed

topics.title: What a 0.25% rate rise does to a home-loan EMI over the years
topics.angle: A small-looking 0.25% costs how much over the loan? Computed from loan amount, rate and tenure.
topics.why_now: Follows the repo hike; searched alongside it.
verify: EMI maths is code-computed; fact reviewer checks that floating loans reset on lender-specific dates

topics.title: Prices rose 5.54% in a year: is your savings account keeping up?
topics.angle: My money sits in a savings account or FD: after September's inflation figure, am I actually earning anything in real terms?
topics.why_now: MoSPI's September CPI (released 12 Oct 2026) jumped to 5.54% from 4.83%, food 7.74%; it also explains why RBI hiked on 7 Oct.

facts.label: All-India retail inflation (CPI, year on year), September
Food inflation (CFPI, year on year), September

verify: MoSPI press release of 12 Oct 2026 (base 2024=100) shows CPI 5.54% (provisional) and CFPI 7.74% for September 2026; August final 4.83%
Savings-account and FD rates are illustrative inputs stated as assumptions, never a named bank's rate
Real return = (1+nominal)/(1+inflation)-1, computed by code; do not call any product a loss-maker outright
Category differs from v-20261016-03 (emergency_fund, 'losing buying power'): tell a duel (savings account vs FD vs inflation), not the same erosion story

topics.title: Will paying by UPI above ₹2,000 cost you extra? What the new merchant fee really is
topics.angle: A shopkeeper refused my UPI payment over ₹2,000 / asked me to pay extra: is there a UPI charge now, and who pays it?
topics.why_now: NPCI's 0.4% merchant fee (MDR) on P2M UPI payments above ₹2,000 was due on 15 Oct and has been deferred until after Diwali; a niche Short on shopkeepers refusing UPI above ₹2,000 got ~40k views in its first 8 hours (market.json, 17 Oct).
verify: NPCI/Finance Ministry: MDR is charged to merchants, not customers; P2P transfers stay free
Proposed scope: 0.4% on P2M payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 from ₹75,000; small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month via QR exempt
Status on the day of the video: confirm whether the rollout is still deferred ('after Diwali', no notified date). If the reviewer can't confirm current status, fail the video
No on-screen figure as a sourced fact unless an official NPCI/PIB page with it is found; rate and threshold may appear only as spoken/explained inputs the reviewer confirms
